title: Four die in Mexico City World Cup celebrations
byline: A 48-year-old woman and a 44-year-old man also died after crowds descended on the city following the country’s 2-0 victory over Ecuador, the capital’s health authority said on Wednesday.

title: Showers likely in Western and hill country areas
byline: The Meteorology Department says a few showers are expected in several parts of the country today (02), while strong winds are likely to prevail in some areas.

title: Israel says troops will stay In Lebanon, Syria, Gaza ’’until further notice’’
byline: Israel’s defence minister said Wednesday that Israeli forces would remain in so-called security zones established in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza ’’until further notice’’.

title: Government launches 23 trilingual public service application forms online
byline: The government on Tuesday launched 23 commonly used public service application forms in Sinhala, Tamil and English, marking a significant step towards improving access to public services and advancing digital governance under the ’Clean Sri Lanka’ programme.

title: Sri Lanka regains upper - middle - income status
byline: Three years after facing what was the worst economic crisis which pushed Sri Lanka to the brink of collapse, the island nation has regained upper-middle-income status.

title: Oil falls for a third straight day after US, Iran talks conclude in Doha
byline: Oil prices dropped about 1% on Thursday, down for a third consecutive day, after Qatar said Iran and the ​U.S. had made progress in indirect talks focused on the Strait of ‌Hormuz, which handled one-fifth of global oil supply before the war.

title: Two killed as bus, three-wheeler collide head-on
byline: A 60-year-old woman and her 13-year-old grandson were killed in a head-on collision between a passenger bus and a three-wheeler on the Galle–Colombo main road in the Katukurunda area in Payagala early Thursday morning.

title: Death sentence imposed twice
byline: An accused has been found guilty of murder twice and sentenced to death by Balapitiya High Court first on February 17, 2026 and then on June 30, 2026. He has been detained at present at the Welikada prison.

title: Sri Lanka looks to Kazakhstan for energy cooperation
byline: Sri Lanka and Kazakhstan have explored opportunities to strengthen cooperation in the energy sector, with Kazakhstan expressing its willingness to support Sri Lanka’s refined fuel requirements during high-level bilateral talks held on Tuesday.

title: Kane the Hero! England escape shock exit as Belgium rally to win
byline: Harry Kane scored twice in the final 15 minutes as England came from behind to beat Congo DR 2-1 and secure a place in the FIFA World Cup Round of 16.

title: Israel says troops will stay In Lebanon, Syria, Gaza ’’until further notice’’
byline: Israel’s defence minister said Wednesday that Israeli forces would remain in so-called security zones established in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza ’’until further notice’’.

title: Sri Lanka courts face over 1 million-case backlog
byline: Sri Lanka’s justice system is under strain, with more than 1.1 million cases pending nationwide, exposing a severe mismatch between caseload and court capacity, Supreme Court Justice Yasantha Kodagoda said.

title: Sri Lanka highlights climate action and SDG integration in Bangkok
byline: Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody has reaffirmed Sri Lanka’s commitment to implementing the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development during his address at the Seventh Global Conference on Climate and SDG Synergies held in Bangkok on 29–30 June 2026.

title: Australia increases student and temporary graduate visa fees
byline: Australia has increased student visa charges, a move set to affect thousands of Kenyan students planning to study in the country or already studying there.

title: Missing young novice monks found safe in Passara
byline: Two young novice monks who were reported missing from the Sri Bodhirukkharama Pirivena Viharaya in Millabedda, Passara, have been found safe, police said.

title: No water tariff revision for next six months: Minister
byline: Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply Susil Ranasinghe said that water tariffs will not be revised for the next six months of this year.

title: India tells WhatsApp to halt usernames rollout, justify feature or face action
byline: India has ​asked WhatsApp to justify the implementation of a planned feature covering usernames and to freeze the rollout ‌in its biggest market, escalating a crackdown on messaging anonymity that began with Telegram, according to a government letter reviewed by Reuters.

title: Pakistan Defence Secretary arrives in Sri Lanka
byline: Secretary of the Ministry of Defence of Pakistan, Lieutenant General (Retd) Muhammad Ali, arrived in Sri Lanka on Wednesday for an official visit to participate in the 6th Pakistan–Sri Lanka Armed Forces Defence Dialogue.

title: Archchuna’s parliamentary eligibility case re-fixed for argument
byline: The writ application challenging the eligibility of Jaffna District Parliamentarian Dr. Ramanathan Archchuna to serve as a Member of Parliament was today re-fixed for argument after the Court of Appeal bench was not properly constituted.

title: Activists demand action as ’AKD Go Home’ slogan returns
byline: Activists associated with the Citizens’ Struggle Movement staged a protest in Borella on Thursday, demanding urgent government action to address the rising cost of living, with demonstrators chanting the slogan ’’AKD Go Home’’ during the protest.

title: Rise in HIV, STIs among Sri Lankan adolescents
byline: Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa raised concerns over a growing number of sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, among adolescents in Sri Lanka, saying the trend has become increasingly evident among both school and university students.

title: S.M. Chandrasena indicted over seed maize distribution case
byline: Former Minister S.M. Chandrasena, who faces corruption allegations, was today served with an indictment before the Colombo High Court after the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption filed charges against him, with the indictment being read before Colombo High Court Judge Ravindra Premaratne.

title: Government paddy purchases delayed as warehouses remain full, farmers’ group claims
byline: The National Agrarians’ Unity has alleged that government purchases of newly harvested paddy in the Northern and Eastern provinces have been delayed because warehouses operated by the Paddy Marketing Board (PMB) remain full of old stocks.

title: Homagama Hospital introduces digital ETU and telemedicine
byline: The Emergency Treatment Unit (ETU) of the Homagama Base Hospital has been digitized, with the hospital also introducing telemedicine services to enable the remote examination and management of patients through video conferencing.

title: Sri Lanka enters El Niño phase, braces for weather extremes
byline: Sri Lanka is currently in the El Niño phase, with weather officials warning that the country could experience a series of extreme weather conditions in the coming months, ranging from reduced rainfall and floods to drought.

title: Russia launches major drone and missile attack on Kyiv
byline: At least eight people were killed and dozens of people were injured after Russian drones and missiles hit residential buildings in Kyiv as part of a broader wave of Russian attacks overnight on the Ukrainian capital.

title: Sri Lanka seeks UNEP support for air quality, plastic waste
byline: Sri Lanka has requested the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) to provide technical and policy support to strengthen the country’s air quality monitoring systems and accelerate efforts to reduce plastic pollution.

title: Sri Lanka named World’s Best Island by Big 7 Travel
byline: Sri Lanka has been ranked the Best Island in the World by global travel platform ’Big 7 Travel’, topping its annual list of ’’The 50 Best Islands in the World’’ for 2026.

title: Bishops’ Conference denies report on extension of Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith’s tenure
byline: The Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Sri Lanka has denied the reports which have been circulating in social media that Archbishop of Colombo Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith has managed to get his tenure extended by using the Easter Sunday bomb attacks.

title: Two arrested over assault on Sri Lanka Air Force officer in Wadduwa
byline: Wadduwa Police have arrested two suspects in connection with the assault on a Sri Lanka Air Force officer near an automated teller machine (ATM) outside a bank branch in Wadduwa, an incident that drew widespread attention on social media.

title: Patients forced to pay triple the cost for essential medicines due to shortages, claims Doctors’ Union
byline: The President of the Medical and Civil Rights Doctors’ Trade Union Alliance, Dr. Chamal Sanjeewa, has alleged that shortages of medicines and surgical equipment in government hospitals and the private healthcare sector have led to patients facing exorbitant costs when purchasing essential medical supplies from private vendors.

title: Fuel cost submissions open until July 14
byline: The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) has called on stakeholders and members of the public to submit written views on the pricing and costing of fuel used for electricity generation on or before 14 July 2026.

title: Mistaken account suspension forces late market opening
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) delayed the commencement of trading yesterday after an exercise to suspend the long-dormant investor accounts inadvertently affected a number of active Central Depository System (CDS) accounts, forcing the market operators to intervene before the opening bell.

title: Plot to overthrow Vijay’s TVK government foiled
byline: The alleged plot to topple the TVK government in Tamil Nadu has blown into an all-out political slugfest, with the TVK and its allies trading charges with the opposition DMK and AIADMK.

title: Hotter inflation unlikely to trigger fresh rate hikes: Bloomberg Economics
byline: Sri Lanka’s inflation is set to climb further through the rest of 2026 but the Central Bank is expected to hold the interest rates steady for the remainder of the year, according to a research note by Bloomberg Economics.

title: No order to remove CID director Shani Abeysekara from Easter Attack investigation
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena today ordered former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director Suresh Sallay, who is being detained and questioned under a Detention Order in connection with the Easter Sunday terrorist attacks, to provide the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) with the passwords to his mobile phone and computer in relation to the investigation conducted into him.

title: Colombo Divisional Secretariats introduce card payment facilities
byline: All 13 Divisional Secretariat Offices in the Colombo District have introduced credit and debit card payment facilities as part of the Government’s drive to modernise public services through digitalisation.

title: Dinal Edirisinghe wins National Table Topics Speech Contest
byline: Dinal Edirisinghe has been crowned the winner of the National Table Topics Speech Contest conducted by District 82 of Toastmasters International at “The Ovation” District Convention held at the Shangri-La Hotel, Colombo.

title: Indonesian couple publicly caned for kissing on TikTok
byline: A young couple in Indonesia’s strict Islamic province of Aceh have been publicly caned for kissing outside marriage on TikTok, an act seen as a violation of Sharia law.

title: Ven Narampanawe Ananda Thero appointed Chancellor of Kelaniya University
byline: The Deputy Chief Prelate of the Asgiriya Chapter, Most Venerable Narampanawe Ananda Thero, has been officially appointed as the new Chancellor of the University of Kelaniya.

title: India to tour Sri Lanka for two-test series in August
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket said that the India men’s cricket team will tour Sri Lanka in August 2026 for a two-match Test series.

title: Dengue outbreak shuts Colombo Visual and Performing Arts University
byline: The University of the Visual and Performing Arts in Colombo has been temporarily shut down following an outbreak of dengue and fever among students, according to the University Grants Commission (UGC).

title: Boy driving pickup truck crashes into group of Thai monks, killing 8
byline: An 11-year-old boy crashed a pickup truck into a group of monks on a pilgrimage walk in northeastern Thailand on Thursday (July 2), killing eight, officials said.

title: Sajith Premadasa congratulates Communist Party of China on 105th anniversary
byline: In a special message marking the 105th anniversary of the Communist Party of China (CPC), Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa extended his warm congratulations, commending the Party’s remarkable transformation and its contribution to China’s emergence as a global economic and technological powerhouse.

title: Withholding A/L results of Muslim candidates over hijab violated fundamental rights: HRCSL
byline: The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) has ruled that the decision to withhold the Advanced Level examination results of around 70 Muslim students from Zahira College, Trincomalee, in 2024 violated their fundamental rights.

title: Notice issued on FCID OIC over request to release electronic devices seized in Krrish investigations
byline: Colombo Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today issued notice on the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID) to present submissions tomorrow regarding a request filed by W.D.N.H. Perera seeking the release of his computers, mobile phones and other electronic devices taken into police custody in connection with investigations into the Krrish transactions.

title: Senior DIG Waruna Jayasundara summoned by CID
byline: Senior Deputy Inspector General (SDIG) of Police for the Eastern Province, Waruna Jayasundara, has been summoned to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for questioning, police sources said.

title: Next indirect US-Iran talks due after late supreme leader’s funeral
byline: The next indirect United States-Iran talks will come after the late Iranian supreme leader’s funeral, mediators said on Thursday (Jul 2), as diplomacy inches ahead on ending the Middle East war.

title: Rise in teen accidents alarms health officials
byline: Health officials have raised concerns over a recent increase in accidents involving teenagers, warning that the growing number of incidents poses a significant risk to public safety.

title: Labour Ministry launches probe into “Mr. Kottu” chain after owner’s arrest
byline: The Ministry of Labour has ordered an urgent investigation into the popular “Mr. Kottu” restaurant chain following the recent arrest of its owner, Viraj Wickramanayake.

title: USA reach World Cup Last 16 as FIFA reports surge in Online Racist Abuse
byline: Football celebrated another World Cup milestone—but away from the pitch, a disturbing surge in online racist abuse cast a dark shadow over the tournament.

title: Historic locomotive move between Kandy and Peradeniya without tracks
byline: A unique operation set to mark a historic moment in Sri Lanka’s railway history is scheduled to be carried out tonight, with a locomotive being transported between Kandy and Peradeniya without using railway tracks.

title: Vehicle importers urges reforms to ease vehicle import process
byline: Vehicle Importers Association of Sri Lanka (VIASL) Vice President Arosha Rodrigo today requested the government to introduce necessary policy adjustments to ensure smoother operations in the sector and to support both importers and buyers.

title: 12-hour water cut in Colombo and suburbs on Saturday
byline: Water supply to several parts of Colombo and surrounding suburbs will be temporarily suspended on Saturday (July 04) from 9.00 a.m. to 9.00 p.m. (12 hours), the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) announced.

title: Canadian boy dies of rabies after waking to bat on his face
byline: An 11-year-old Canadian boy has died from rabies after being awoken by a bat on his nose and mouth.

title: Gazette amends colour-coded labelling rules for sugary drinks
byline: An Extraordinary Gazette Notification has been issued amending the regulations on colour-coded labelling for sugar-containing liquid food products.

title: CSE ends slightly lower as early gains fade amid selective buying and weak sentiment
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) opened the session on a positive note, with the ASPI gaining around 60 points during the first hour of trading, supported by early buying interest across selected counters.

title: Commission launched to tackle public sector pay issues
byline: The newly appointed Salary and Pension Commission, established by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to address long-standing salary and pension issues in the public service, officially commenced its work with its inaugural meeting held yesterday (July 1) at the Nilamadura premises in Narahenpita.

title: Fake inland revenue officer arrested for alleged tax scam
byline: A man accused of impersonating an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) official and defrauding taxpayers and institutions across Sri Lanka has been arrested following an investigation conducted by the Company Street Police and officials of the Inland Revenue Department.

title: 70% of prison population linked to drug addiction, overcrowding concerns raised
byline: Around 70 per cent of the prison population comprises individuals addicted to narcotic substances, highlighting a major challenge facing the country’s correctional system, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: 225 awareness programmes conducted to protect schoolchildren from drug use
byline: Efforts to prevent schoolchildren from being drawn into drug use have intensified, with officials reporting that 225 awareness programmes have already been carried out for teachers and students across schools, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Visiting Pakistan Defence Secretary holds talks with Sri Lankan counterpart
byline: Pakistan’s Secretary of the Ministry of Defence, Lieutenant General (Retd) Muhammad Ali, paid a courtesy call on Sri Lanka’s Defence Secretary, Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha (Retd), at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters in Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte.
